summary.text: A 14-year-old female domestic shorthaired cat with subcutaneous ureteral bypass systems, placed for bilateral obstructive ureteroliths, presented for a flush of the systems after a few days of lethargy, hyporexia and small amounts of grossly normal urine. History included hyperthyroidism treated with radioactive iodine, stable Stage II chronic renal disease and idiopathic hypercalcemia.

Urine from the SUB systems contained 100-150 leukocytes per hpf and heavy growth of E. coli, phenotypically resistant to all tested penicillins, cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines, sulfonamides and chloramphenicol. The infection was ESBL E. coli ST162 with CTX-M-14, with a presumptive diagnosis of pyelonephritis because pyelocentesis could not be performed.

The cat received meropenem 9.7 mg/kg SC q12h for 8 weeks and was successfully treated, with urine cultures at 4, 8, 11, 15 and 20 weeks showing no bacterial growth. It was euthanized 6 months after the E. coli diagnosis for progressive azotemia believed unrelated to the infection.

summary.text: A 16-year-old male mixed-breed dog presented with vomiting, inappetence and fever about 7 months after the cat in the same household was diagnosed with an E. coli urinary tract infection. It had stable Stage I chronic renal disease and two episodes of idiopathic vestibular disease in the preceding 3 months, from which it fully recovered.

Examination showed faintly icteric sclera and serum chemistry showed increased liver enzymes and total bilirubin consistent with hepatobiliary disease. Bile obtained by ultrasound-guided cholecystocentesis contained rod-shaped bacteria and cultured heavy growth of E. coli and Clostridium perfringens; the E. coli was resistant to many drug classes. Cholangiohepatitis caused by E. coli ST162 with CTX-M-14 was diagnosed.

Treatment began with amoxicillin-clavulanate pending culture, then changed to meropenem and metronidazole for 3 weeks. Bile culture after completing dual therapy showed no bacterial growth. The dog was lost to follow-up because of owner relocation.
